newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli insurance companies fined over cartel.
newsitem.headline: Israeli insurance companies fined over cartel.

text.p: An Israeli court on Friday imposed suspended jail terms and fines on seven insurance companies and their heads for forming a cartel to fix insurance premiums, Itim news agency reported.
Fines of 6.6 million shekels ($2 million) each were imposed on the country's two biggest insurance companies, Migdal, a subsidiary of Leumi Insurance Holdings, and Clal Insurance Holdings.
Their managing directors, Uzi Levy of Migdal and Rimon Ben-Shaul of Clal, were sentenced to suspended jail terms of one year and fined 300,000 shekels ($89,285) each.
Assicurazioni Generali SpA is about to buy control of Migdal's parent company, Leumi Insurance.
Jerusalem District Court Judge Yonatan Adiel said the jail terms go into effect if the convicted men repeat the crime in the next three years, Itim said.

Other companies and their managing directors received smaller fines and shorter suspended jail terms. The Israel Insurance Association was fined one million shekels ($300,000) for involvement in the cartel.
The judge said the companies fixed premiums, coordinated rates and limited discounts to policy holders in commercial and home-owners insurance, in violation of a restrictive business practice law.

The accused were convicted based on their admissions of guilt as part of a plea bargain. The judge said he gave the heaviest sentences possible under the law governing plea bargains, saying "the practices harmed not just individuals but the whole public," Itim reported.
However, he said it was impossible to know just how much the public was harmed.
